chunks: He said, and Bakr ibn Salih narrated to us from Bundar ibn Muhammad al-Tabari from Ali ibn Suwayd al-Sa'i from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'Advise me.' He said, 'I order you with the fear of Allah.' Then he was silent, so I complained to him about the scarcity of what was in my hand, and I said, 'By Allah, I have become naked, and my nakedness reached such an extent that Abu so-and-so removed two garments that were upon him and clothed me with them.' He said, 'Fast and give charity.' I said, 'Can I give charity from what has reached me from my brethren, even if it is little?' He said, 'Give charity from what Allah has provided you with, even if you have to prefer (others) over yourself.'
ai.seo_question: How can one give charity when they are poor?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (AS) responds to the narrator's complaint of poverty by prescribing fasting and charity, specifically instructing him to give from what he received from others even if it is small. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ithar* (preferring others) as a practical spiritual discipline, where one sacrifices personal comfort to fulfill divine command, regardless of the scale of wealth.

en.hubeali: He said, ‘And Bakr Bin Salih narrated to us, from Bundar Bin Muhammad Al Tabary, from Ali Bin Suweyd Al Sa’aiy, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Advise me’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> order you with the fear of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> was silent, so I complained to him<sup>asws</sup> of the scarcity of what was in my hands, and I said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I have become naked, and my nakedness reached to such an extent that Abu so and so removed two clothes which were upon him, and clothed me with these two’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Fast and give charity’. I said, ‘Can I give in charity from what has arrived to me from my brethren, and even if it was little?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Give charity from what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Graced you with, even though you have to prefer (others) over yourself’.
en.sarwar: 2. The narrator of the above Hadith has said that narrated to us Bakr ibn Salih from Bandar ibn Muhammad al-Tabariy from Ali ibn Suwayd al-Sa’iy who has said the following:

“I once said to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Please instruct me with good advice.’ He said, ‘I advise you to observe piety before Allah.’ He was silent for a while. I then complained to him about my poverty, saying, ‘By Allah, I do not have any clothes, and it is so much that abu so and so took off two pieces of his clothes so I can wear them.’ He said, ‘Fast and give charity.’ I then asked, ‘Should I give charity from what my friends have given to me, even if it is so little?’ He replied, ‘Give charity from what Allah has provided you, even if you have to give preference to others over yourself.’”
